content.title: About
content.content: Strawberry shortcake is a light sponge cake soaked with fresh strawberry syrup and topped with whipped cream and sliced strawberries. The dessert is popular in the summer and often served at celebrations and parties.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic shortcake originated in the United States in the early 1920s and quickly became a beloved summer dessert.
Strawberries not only add aroma but also natural sweetness, allowing the recipe to use less added sugar.
The sponge layer is usually made without butter, making it lighter than typical cakes.
Whipped cream is often flavored with a hint of vanilla extract to enhance the taste.
Strawberry shortcake is frequently decorated with edible flowers, making it a favorite at wedding receptions.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Strawberries provide a high amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The sponge cake is prepared without added butter, reducing saturated fat content per serving.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Fresh berries and whole‑grain sponge contribute dietary fiber beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Strawberries are rich in anthocyanins, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Calcium from cream
items.content: Whipped cream adds calcium, essential for bone health.

items.title: Strawberry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to strawberries, such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The syrup and cream can increase the overall sugar level, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Strawberries are acidic and may irritate a sensitive stomach in people with gastritis.

items.title: Lactose content
items.content: Whipped cream contains lactose, making the dessert unsuitable for those with lactose intolerance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve strawberry shortcake chilled. Slice into portions, garnish with extra berries and a dusting of powdered sugar. It pairs well with a cup of black coffee or fruit tea.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the shortcake in the refrigerator, covered with plastic wrap or in an airtight container, for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a separate bag and thaw in the fridge before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: The frozen yogurt bar with vanilla flavor is a chilled dessert made from smooth yogurt, lightly sweetened and infused with natural vanilla. It offers a creamy texture, a mild sweetness, and lower fat content compared with traditional ice cream.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The yogurt base provides live probiotic cultures that support gut health.
Vanilla flavor can come from real vanilla beans or natural extracts in large‑scale production.
Freezing retains most of the protein present in regular yogurt.
Bars are portable and require no utensils.
In some markets the bars are coated with a thin layer of dark chocolate for extra crunch.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Yogurt contains live bacterial cultures that help maintain a healthy intestinal microbiome.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with traditional ice cream, frozen yogurt typically contains less saturated fat.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Yogurt is a good source of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The bar provides a moderate amount of protein, contributing to satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yogurt supplies B12 and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People who are lactose intolerant may experience discomfort after consuming yogurt.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to milk proteins.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although moderately sweet, the bar still contains added sugar, which should be considered by diabetics or those on low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Melting storage
items.content: If stored above –18 °C for extended periods, the texture can become icy and grainy.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bar straight from the wrapper, let it soften for a smoother bite, or crumble it over fruit salads, granola, and smoothies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at –18 °C or lower. Once removed from the package, consume within about 30 minutes to avoid ice crystal formation on the surface.

content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑sugar jam and jelly are fruit preserves in which the amount of added sugar is cut to about 30 % of the traditional level. They retain the bright fruit flavor while containing fewer calories, making them suitable for people monitoring sugar intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The lower sugar content is achieved by using concentrated fruit purées and natural sweeteners.
Traditional jam uses a 1:1 sugar‑to‑fruit ratio; reduced‑sugar versions typically use about 1:3.
Jelly often relies on pectin to achieve the right set without large amounts of sugar.
Reduced sugar helps preserve more vitamins and antioxidants that can degrade with high‑heat, high‑sugar cooking.
These products are popular among athletes and people with diabetes, though the glycemic index should still be checked.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Fruit purée in the jam retains vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Skin and pulp of the fruit provide fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Lower glycemic impact
items.content: Reduced sugar leads to a slower rise in blood glucose levels.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols from berries help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: The water content in the product contributes to overall fluid balance.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to specific berries or fruits used in the jam.

items.title: Artificial sweetener content
items.content: Certain reduced‑sugar versions use sucralose or aspartame, which may be undesirable for sensitive consumers.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: With less sugar acting as a preservative, the product may spoil faster after opening.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread reduced‑sugar jam or jelly on toast, use it in baking, stir into yogurt, oatmeal or smoothies. It also works well as a filling for pancakes, waffles, and crepes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. After opening, refrigerate and consume within 2–3 weeks. Discard if mold appears or the smell changes.

content.title: About
content.content: Passion fruit juice, 100% is a completely natural beverage made from ripe passion fruit (Passiflora edulis). It has a bright aroma, sweet‑tart flavor, and is rich in vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Passion fruit originates from tropical South America but is now cultivated in Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean.
The juice is widely used in sauces, desserts, and cocktails.
Passion fruit contains over 30 % dietary fiber, supporting digestive health.
Its tropical scent is often associated with summer vacation drinks.
Passion fruit juice is also used in cosmetics for its moisturizing and soothing properties.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis, improving skin health.

items.title: Contains vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A is essential for vision and the health of mucous membranes.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes regular bowel movements and may reduce constipation.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to passion fruit.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although the juice is 100% natural, inherent sugars can affect blood glucose levels.

items.title: Quality control
items.content: Choose juice without added preservatives or artificial flavors.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice chilled, use it in smoothies, cocktails, marinades, sauces for fish and seafood, as well as in desserts and yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the juice in the refrigerator at 0 °C to 4 °C. After opening, consume within 3–5 days. Avoid freezing, as it may alter flavor and texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Pepper steak is a dish of thinly sliced beef quickly stir‑fried with bell peppers, onion and soy sauce. It is popular in Asian cuisine, especially Chinese and Thai, and is often served over rice or noodles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish appeared in the United States in the mid‑20th century as an adaptation of Chinese "chow fan".
Traditionally tender cuts such as sirloin or tenderloin are used so the meat stays juicy during fast cooking.
The sweet soy sauce combined with spicy pepper creates a characteristic sweet‑savory balance.
Variations may include carrots, mushrooms, pineapple or toasted cashews.
High‑heat cooking preserves the crisp texture of the vegetables.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from beef supports hemoglobin formation and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish supplies B12, B6 and niacin, which are important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from peppers
items.content: Bell peppers are rich in vitamin C and carotenoids that combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: With vegetables as the main carbohydrate source, pepper steak fits well into low‑carb diets.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce adds a lot of salt; people with hypertension should limit the amount.

items.title: Overcooking
items.content: Cooking the meat too long can make it tough and generate harmful compounds.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked beef may contain pathogens such as E. coli.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice beef thinly, marinate in soy sauce, ginger and garlic for 15‑30 minutes. Stir‑fry quickly over high heat with sliced bell peppers and onion, then add a sauce made from soy sauce, sugar and cornstarch. Serve hot over rice or noodles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh beef should be kept in the refrigerator for up to 2 days, while the cooked dish can be stored in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Marinated beef can be frozen for up to 3 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Gatorade G2 is a low‑calorie sports drink designed to replenish electrolytes and maintain hydration during intense workouts. It provides about 20 kcal per 240 ml serving, roughly five times fewer calories than regular Gatorade.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: G2 was first launched in the United States in 2004 as a response to growing demand for "light" sports beverages.
Unlike the original Gatorade, G2 contains less sugar (about 5 g per serving) and replaces part of it with artificial sweeteners.
The drink is fortified with electrolytes—sodium and potassium—in a ratio that supports rapid recovery after sweat loss.
G2 is available in several flavors, including lemon‑lime, berry blend, and orange.
It is commonly sold in 500 ml bottles, making it convenient to take to the gym.

items.title: Electrolyte Replenishment
items.content: Sodium and potassium help restore electrolyte balance, reducing the risk of cramps and fatigue.

items.title: Low Calorie Content
items.content: Only about 20 kcal per serving allows hydration without a significant caloric load.

items.title: Hydration Support
items.content: The drink’s osmolality is optimized for rapid water absorption.

items.title: B‑vitamin Content
items.content: Vitamins B3 and B6 aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: No Artificial Colors
items.content: G2 uses natural flavorings, making it more acceptable for sensitive consumers.

items.title: Artificial Sweeteners
items.content: Some individuals may experience gastrointestinal discomfort from sweeteners such as sucralose.

items.title: Sodium Content
items.content: People advised to limit sodium intake should account for the drink’s sodium levels.

items.title: Allergy to Ingredients
items.content: Rare allergic reactions to flavorings or preservatives can occur.

items.title: Not a Meal Replacement
items.content: G2 is intended for post‑exercise recovery, not as a primary source of nutrition.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Consume Gatorade G2 15‑30 minutes before a workout or immediately after, diluting 240 ml with water if desired. It pairs well with light protein‑rich snacks for more complete recovery.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, refrigerate and consume within 24 hours.
